claims.text: Standard L-PBF processing of cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi typically generates thermal gradients.
Thermal gradients during standard L-PBF lead to segregation in AlCrFeNiSi.
Thermal gradients during standard L-PBF lead to residual stresses in AlCrFeNiSi.
Thermal gradients during standard L-PBF lead to defect formation in AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed intervention combines controlled laser-path rotation, exemplified by 90° rotation between successive layers, with reduced hatch spacing corresponding to 60–80% overlap.
The scan parameters will be selected through a design-of-experiments approach.
The proposed scan strategy will produce a more uniform distribution of heat across the build.
More uniform heat distribution will create a more even melt pool and a better-controlled solidification front.
An even melt pool and controlled solidification front will minimize localized overheating and undercooling.
The improved scanning strategy will reduce thermal gradients.
Reduced thermal gradients will reduce microsegregation.
Reduced thermal gradients will reduce residual-stress formation.
A uniform thermal profile will promote consistent layer bonding and a homogenized microstructure.
Consistent layer bonding and a homogenized microstructure will enhance mechanical integrity.
Compared with conventional L-PBF scanning, the optimized strategy will yield significantly lower residual stresses.
Compared with conventional L-PBF scanning, the optimized strategy will reduce segregation at interlayer boundaries.
Compared with conventional L-PBF scanning, the optimized strategy will produce fewer process-induced defects.
Compared with conventional L-PBF scanning, the optimized strategy will improve overall mechanical performance.
The predicted improvements are limited to standard L-PBF build geometries, layer thicknesses, and controlled ambient processing conditions.
Theoretical and preliminary evidence supports reduced thermal gradients and improved microstructural uniformity.
